seams.reasonForTopChoice: Close asks for guidance on the straight path; D answers: this scripture, beyond doubt, guides the mindful.
Belief in all the books is continued by a scripture confirming earlier ones, with believers affirming all of it.
Close ends exhorting believers to fear God to succeed; B opens telling people to fear their Lord and continues practical community duties.
Close gives a legal ruling clarified by God for believers; E continues with further binding rules and obligations addressed to believers.
Close ends with God ruling heavens, earth and all within; E opens praising God who made heavens and earth, against those setting up equals.
Close refuses any lord but God and warns of swift punishment; B says follow no other patrons and recalls towns destroyed, deeds weighed.
Close urges silent listening and humble remembrance; E describes true believers whose hearts tremble at God's mention and whose faith grows on hearing verses.
Continues the subject of treaties and relations with deniers by announcing terms for treaty-bound idolaters.
Close announces a messenger from among yourselves; A asks whether it is strange that one of them was inspired to warn.
Close: call on none but God, truth has come, I am not your guardian; C: worship only God, speaker merely warns and brings good news.
The close says messengers' accounts are told to steady the heart; this opens by telling the best of stories.
Close says the stories are no invention but confirmation, lessons for the thoughtful; B affirms what is revealed is truth, with signs for thinkers.
Answers the charge of being no messenger: a scripture sent through him, as every messenger was sent.
Close says God keeps His promise and warns He is one God; B says God's command is coming and angels warn He alone is god.
Close ends: worship until certainty comes, with mockers answered; C opens that God's command is coming, do not hurry it.
The advice not to grieve over them is echoed by the warning against destroying oneself with grief.
Close ends praising God who has no child; A opens with praise to God and warns those claiming He took a child.
Close says I am only a human like you and speaks of the Lord's words; B has deniers objecting he is merely human like them.
Close rejects ascribing a child to God and says the message gladdens and warns; A warns child-claimers and promises believers reward.
Close has them demanding a sign and everyone waiting; D says reckoning nears while they are heedless and still demand a sign.
Close warns all, unsure if the promise is near or far; B opens by telling people to fear the terrible final hour.
Believers urged to pray, give alms and do good are then declared successful for exactly those traits.
Close exalts God the true king and condemns invoking another god; B blesses the ruler of heavens and earth and rejects powerless adopted gods.
God owning everything and the messenger's standing continue into His rule of heavens and earth and His servant's warning.
Picks up the same portrait of the faithful: shunning idle talk, spouses, and an eternal reward in paradise.
After denying the message comes from devils or poets, E presents it as a clear book guiding believers, with deniers wandering blindly like the poets.
Reciting the scripture, warning the stray, and promised signs continue in clear verses, grief over unbelief, and a sign.
Returning to God and not siding with unbelievers leads into believers being tested and meeting God.
Close promises guidance to those who strive and condemns belief in falsehood; C offers guidance for good-doers against one who buys idle tales to mislead.
Deniers rejecting the scripture's signs are followed by one who turns from its verses with idle tales.
Close ends on God alone knowing the hour, rain and wombs; E continues with what God knows of earth and sky and the denied hour.
Close has them asking when the decision will come; A has deniers saying the hour will not come and an oath that it will.
Close mentions heavens and earth, punishment and mercy to believers; C praises the owner of heaven and earth who rewards believers by exact record.
Close declares truth has come by revelation and ends with doubters; C declares the scripture undoubtedly from the Lord, truth not invention.
Continues arrogance, scheming, perished earlier generations, and punishment not yet tasted because deferred.
Close argues the maker of heavens and earth can re-create man; B asks whether they are harder to create, being made from clay.
Picks up the reminder, the defiant deniers, earlier generations, and punishment they have not yet tasted.
Close has a fire-made being scorning clay, expelled and cursed; A has devils pelted and driven off, and people made from sticky clay.
Close ends with angels circling the throne in praise; E opens with angels praising God and seeking forgiveness for those on earth.
Close: stronger earlier peoples exulted, then believed too late; A: proud deniers, earlier generations perished crying out too late.
If this is from God and rejected: the scripture is from God, and only deniers dispute His signs.
Close says God speaks to a human by inspiration or from behind a veil; E has a veil between and a human inspired.
Close leaves them to play until their promised day; D says they play in doubt and tells him to watch for the day.
Close contrasts hell and gardens and says it was eased in your tongue; C has recitation in a named language warning of garden and blaze.
Close ends praising God after deniers ignored the hour; D presents scripture from the creator of heavens and earth, deniers ignoring the warning.
Deniers' fate and why punishment is not hastened continue: God voids their deeds and tests people by one another.
Close urges not weakening while uppermost and promises reward; D announces a clear victory and tranquillity sent into believers' hearts.
Close describes the messenger's companions and promises forgiveness and great reward; A instructs them on conduct toward him with the same promise.
God's favor in guiding to faith continues as favor completed, guidance, and faith deepened in believers' hearts.
Close ends with the day of coming forth and God's warning; D swears that the promise is true and judgement will come.
Close ends with woe to unbelievers on their promised day; E swears the punishment will fall and repeats woe to deniers, with the magic taunt.
Close ends with praise as the stars fade; A opens with an oath by the setting star and vindicates the companion.
Close says the imminent event nears and a warner has come; C opens that the hour nears and warnings fail.
Close says everything is created by measure and ends near a mighty King; A names the Merciful, sun and moon reckoned, the balance set.
Close describes gardens with people reclining on cushions; E sorts people into groups, the foremost reclining on couches in gardens of delight.
The command to glorify the Lord is answered by everything glorifying God, giver of life and death, ever near.
The closing mention of scripture-holders is picked up by the account of deniers among them being expelled.
Directly continues the ban on befriending those who oppose God and His messenger.
Close lists God as king, holy, glorified by heaven and earth; A opens with everything glorifying the holy king, then scripture carried or not.
Close has a pledge and a ban on allying with God's enemies; A rebukes saying without doing and praises fighting for God in ranks.
The promised near victory and believers prevailing over refusers is illustrated by deniers driven from their homes.
Those who desert the messenger for trade lead into insincere followers whose testimony to him is false.
Might belonging to God leads into His kingship and power; believers versus deniers and hidden hearts continue.
Close warns about spouses and urges fearing God; B gives rules for parting from wives and promises a way out to the God-mindful.
Close ends with seven heavens showing God's power over everything; D opens with the holder of all power who made seven flawless heavens.
Close gives examples of prophets' wives and marriage loyalty; C continues with the prophet addressed on wives and divorce conduct.
Answers the question of when the promised punishment comes: unstoppable for deniers, and seen as near.
Close urges patience while deniers are given time; C repeats the call to patience and announces the punishment sure to befall them.
Close defends the messenger as no poet or soothsayer; C continues the defence, swearing he is not mad and urging him not to yield.
Close leaves deniers until their promised day and threatens replacing them; D names the inevitable and recounts earlier peoples wiped out.
Close tells of a people drowned for clinging to idols; C lists destroyed peoples and recalls being carried by ship when water overflowed.
Near or far is answered directly: they see the promised punishment as far, God sees it near.
Close addresses the night-worshipper with commands to pray, give and lend; C addresses him again to rise, warn, give without gain and be patient.
Close has the damned admitting they denied judgment day; D swears by the day of rising and answers man's doubt about it.
Close asks if man is left purposeless, recalling the drop he came from; B answers: made from a drop in order to test him.
Close calls itself a reminder and warns of a neglected heavy day; B swears by bearers of a reminder that the promised day will happen.
Close asks what message they will believe and names the day of sorting; B has them disputing the great news, the day of decision fixed.
Close warns of the day each sees what his hands sent ahead; E depicts that day, when each soul knows what it brought.
Close has people asking when the hour comes and mentions anchored mountains; A opens with people asking about the great news, mountains as pegs.
Close ends with the cry when each abandons kin, absorbed in himself; E continues that day's scenes, things abandoned, each soul knowing what it brought.
Repeats the image of stars and of each soul learning what it did, with noble recorders.
Recorded deeds, the wicked, and denial of judgment day continue in the wicked's register and woe to deniers.
Close has believers watching deniers who once mocked them; E shows persecutors sitting and watching what they did to believers, then requital.
Close has celestial oaths and punishment except for believers who do good; C continues sky oaths, burning for persecutors and gardens for such believers.
Close: God witnesses, begins and repeats, guarded recitation, deniers surrounded; C: every soul has a watcher, God restores man, decisive speech, deniers given respite.
Close reflects on man's creation and decisive speech, leaving deniers aside; A turns to glorifying the Lord who creates and shapes, then reciting and reminding.
The better hereafter and the two fates are unfolded: faces in fire and faces in the garden.
Repeats the command to remind, and the fate of the one who turns away into great fire.
Close rebukes intense love of wealth and regret at sending nothing ahead; B rebukes boasting of squandered wealth and neglecting to feed the needy.
Close contrasts squandered wealth with the steep path of giving, two ways, fire; D contrasts the giver and the miser whose wealth is useless.
Continues oaths by night and day, the purifying of oneself, and the fate of the wretched denier.
Repeats the promise that he will be satisfied, with giving to the poor and not repelling beggars.
Close lists God's favours to the listener; B continues the same list: chest opened, burden lifted, renown raised, ease after hardship.
Close reassures the listener by recalling favours; E is the same kind of reassurance, recounting shelter, guidance and enrichment from his Lord.
Continues man's creation, his overstepping decline, and the return to the Lord who judges.
Close commands reading what God taught; E continues with how it was sent down, on the night of decree.
Close tells of the revelation being sent down; B tells what followed when that clear proof came, a messenger reciting purified pages.
The two fates, pleased believers and deniers in fire, are mirrored by heavy scales and light scales.
Scattered people and atom-weights of deeds lead into scattered moths and the weighing of scales.
Close ends with graves emptied and hearts' contents exposed; C shows earth throwing out its burdens and people shown their deeds.
The raging fire for light scales continues as the blazing fire seen with certainty and the questioning.
Rivalry in piling up continues as the wealth-counter, who is thrown into God's kindled fire.
Shows the loss in concrete form: the backbiter hoarding wealth, opposite of those urging truth and patience.
Close condemns the wealth-hoarder bound for the fire; D rebukes rivalry in piling up more and warns they will see the blazing fire.
Close tells of an attacking army destroyed; D follows with a tribe's resulting security, owed to the Lord who made them safe from fear.
Close asks worship of the Lord who fed them against hunger; D condemns those who neglect feeding the poor and pray heedlessly.
Close condemns careless, showy prayer and withholding help; A gives the contrast: pray to your Lord sincerely and sacrifice from abundance.
The hater who is cut off without a future is matched by a man cursed and ruined.
Close separates two religions; A shows the outcome, people entering God's religion in crowds when help and victory arrive.
Close: victory granted, so glorify your Lord; A parallels it: abundance granted, so pray to your Lord, and the enemy is cut off.
After cursing a doomed opponent whose wealth is useless, B turns to address the deniers directly and separates from their worship.
After declaring God the one on whom all depend, one seeks refuge with Him as Lord, King, God.
Close is a refuge prayer against outer harms; A is its twin refuge prayer, against the inner whisperer.
